thread:
Eli: Heads-up — saw a multi-second config propagation lag on private VPC canary yesterday. Some nodes never got the split update.
Maria: timeline?
Eli: 1791232200-ish we pushed a 5->20% traffic split. Console showed success, but kube-agent logs on a few hosts show older config persisted.
Sam: do you have logs? can you paste the agent apply errors?
Eli: pasted below:
```
2026-01-26T18:12:34Z agent[svc]: fetch-config 200 OK
2026-01-26T18:12:34Z agent[svc]: apply-config v2 -> v3
2026-01-26T18:12:34Z agent[svc]: apply failed: anchor-cert not found, retrying
2026-01-26T18:12:40Z agent[svc]: apply succeeded
```
Jess: anchor-cert? that's the offline cert we use for air-gapped control plane sync, might mean bundle lagged.
Maria: hmm. This is the classic push vs pull problem — in VPC we rely on the control plane to push delta bundles to the edge relay, but in air-gapped installs they pull from the package server on a schedule.
Sam: what was our rollout guard? heartbeat + quorum in 2m window?
Eli: current guard: require success on 60% hosts in region within 90s, else automatic rollback. But the console immediately marked route active when control-plane returned 200.
Jess: that's the bug — console considers control-plane acceptance, not host apply state. We need to surface host-side apply SLO before marking the traffic split live.
Maria: Agreed. Two practical fixes: (1) make control-plane accept only after N host ACKs (blocking commit) OR (2) keep current optimistic commit but mark route as 'pending-host-apply' and gate actual routing in the dataplane until host ACKs arrive.
Sam: (2) is safer for air-gapped — don't depend on synchronous host ACKs.
Eli: Also need a UX change: the rollout timeline should show per-region host ack progress and expected ETA. Right now the spinner is meaningless.
Jess: For VPC/private, certificate rotation can delay apply. Could we extend agent backoff jitter and bump guard timeout for private installs? Ops might not like longer failover windows.
Maria: Instead of lengthening global timeout, make timeouts policy-driven per-install-type: airgapped=true => host-ack-timeout=5m, else 90s.
Sam: Also add a 'soft-split' mode where new hosts get mirrored traffic percentage but not counted in success quorum until they report healthy. That lets us start shadowing new variant without impacting latency-sensitive production.
Eli: Nice. We also need to avoid thundering herd when many hosts pull for bundles. Suggest randomized pull schedule + per-host jitter and staggered rollout seeds.
Jess: Agreed. Also add deterministic rollout tokens in the control plane so traffic hashing is stable across partial rollouts. Currently we had hashing drift when config version changed mid-fanout.
Maria: Implementation checklist:
- [ ] change console commit state machine to 'control-plane-accepted' vs 'host-applied'
- [ ] add per-install-type guard timeout config
- [ ] implement soft-split shadowing mode
- [ ] surface per-host ACK progress in rollout timeline
Sam: I'll take the control-plane state machine change. @Jess take soft-split? @Maria can you do UX for the timeline?
Jess: taking soft-split. Will sketch API changes. quick proto for rollout payload:
```
{
  "rollout_id": "r-20260126-001",
  "target": "model-a@v3",
  "traffic_policy": {
    "type": "soft_split",
    "splits": [{"variant":"v3","pct":20}, {"variant":"v2","pct":80}],
    "host_ack_timeout": "5m"
  }
}
```
Eli: also add a control-plane health check that refuses commits if relay queue > X or last-agent-poll > Y.
Maria: Good guard. Deploy-bot: canary started notification?
deploy-bot: canary(r-20260126-001) started at 2026-01-26T18:12:33Z — traffic 20% target. monitoring: rolling.
Sam: great. Let's also add telemetry hooks: per-host apply latencies, cert errors counter, and rollout-stability metric (fraction of rollouts hitting host-apply mismatch).
Eli: thanks all. I'll open a GH issue linking this thread, with the checklist and assign prs.
Jess: thanks — will post API sketch by EOD. :thumbsup:
Maria: FYI ops asked that we include opt-out flag for customer-managed relays (they don't want blocking commits). We'll add policy field.
Eli: noted. We'll keep default conservative but allow opt-out. Closing for now.
